subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should plain `message.send` prevent models from seeing poll content fields, strip accidental poll fields at runtime, or keep rejecting content-bearing poll fields as explicit poll intent?
rationale: The current code intentionally accepts metadata-only padding but still rejects non-empty poll content fields; changing that boundary affects the shared model-facing message-tool contract across multiple channels.

options.title: Action-scope poll fields
options.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

options.title: Strip on send
options.body: Treat `action="send"` as authoritative and drop poll creation fields before delivery, improving reliability but potentially hiding wrong-action callers.

options.title: Keep strict guard
options.body: Continue rejecting content-bearing poll fields on send and require stronger live evidence before changing the tool contract further.

recommendation.title: Action-scope poll fields
recommendation.body: Expose poll creation fields only for poll actions or channel-specific poll tools, reducing accidental model fill while preserving strict poll validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their poll gating and schema-consistency history is the strongest signal for the shared send/poll contract boundary.
